'''Andrew Dawson Taylor''' (born 1950<ref name=whoswho/>) was director of the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]] National Laboratories<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref> – [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]],<ref name="SeegerTaylor1985">{{cite journal|last1=Seeger|first1=P.A.|last2=Taylor|first2=A.D.|last3=Brugger|first3=R.M.|title=Double-difference method to improve the resolution of an eV neutron spectrometer|journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment|volume=240|issue=1|year=1985|pages=98–114|issn=0168-9002|doi=10.1016/0168-9002(85)90392-4|bibcode=1985NIMPA.240...98S }}</ref><ref name=isis>{{cite journal|last1=Taylor|first1=Andrew|title=Welcome to the second target station at ISIS|journal=Materials Today|volume=11|issue=12|year=2008|pages=72|issn=1369-7021|doi=10.1016/S1369-7021(08)70259-1|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Daresbury Laboratory]], and the [[UK Astronomy Technology Centre]] in [[Edinburgh]]<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424064106/https://royalsociety.org/people/andrew-taylor-14129/|archivedate=24 April 2019|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/andrew-taylor-14129/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2019|title=Dr Andrew Taylor OBE FRS}} One or more of ==Education==
Taylor was educated at [[Denny High School]], the [[University of Glasgow]]<ref name=whoswho/> and the [[University of Oxford]] where he was a postgraduate student of [[St John's College, Oxford]].<ref name=whoswho/> He was awarded a Doctor of Philosophy degree in 1976 for research using [[inelastic neutron scattering]].<ref name=PhD-474621>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/permalink/f/89vilt/oxfaleph019872832|title=Inelastic Neutron Scattering by Chemical Rate Processes|first= Andrew Dawson|last=Taylor|year=1976|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.474621}}|publisher=University of Oxford|oclc=500576530}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Taylor's research interests are in [[neutron]] science, [[neutron source]]s<ref name=science/> and [[neutron scattering]],<ref name=scopus/><ref name=telegraph/> he is recognised as an international leader in the development of large-scale research facilities and their infrastructures.<ref name=frs/>

===Awards and honours===
Taylor was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2019 for "substantial contributions to the improvement of natural knowledge".<ref name=elections>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906183433/https://royalsociety.org/fellows/elections/|website=royalsociety.org |archivedate=6 September 2015|url=https://royalsociety.org/fellows/elections/ |publisher=Royal Society|location=London|title=Royal Society Elections|author=Anon|year=2015}}</ref> He was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[1999 Birthday Honours]]<ref name=whoswho/><ref name=ukri>{{Cite web|url=https://stfc.ukri.org/news/stfc-director-honoured-by-the-royal-society/|author=Anon|year=2019|title=STFC director honoured by the Royal Society|website=stfc.ukri.org|publisher=Science and Technology Facilities Council}}</ref><ref name=telegraph>{{Cite web|location=London|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/jobs/5314222/Andrew-Taylor-profile-Neutron-man-grapples-with-the-invisibles.html|title=Andrew Taylor profile: Neutron man grapples with the invisibles|first=Roland|last=Gribben|date=13 May 2009|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20191111124048/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/jobs/5314222/Andrew-Taylor-profile-Neutron-man-grapples-with-the-invisibles.html|archivedate=11 November 2019}}</ref> and [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2020 New Year Honours]] for services to science and technology.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=62866|supp=y|page=N10|date=28 December 2019}}</ref> He was also elected a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] (FInstP){{when|date=November 2019}} and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE) in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/andrew-taylor-2/|location=Edinburgh|title=Dr Andrew Dawson Taylor OBE, FRS, FRSE|website=rse.org.uk|year=2006|author=Anon|publisher=[[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Richard Glazebrook Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]] in 2006.
